corrections.original: On 2026-10-14, after the text layout left the program, it was 4,254 live operations in 123 layers. / Removing the text layout and merging two windows brought it down to 4,254 in 123 layers on 2026-10-14. / Curiosity hook: 21,229 -> 4,254 in one day.
corrections.fix: The text layout left on the evening of 2026-10-13: 19,851 -> 4,251 live operations, 217 -> 123 layers, 8,959 weights (the window merge, 21,229 -> 19,851, came earlier the same day). 4,254 live / 8,965 weights is 2026-10-14, after Monitor's 64-slot row rule added 3 ops. The one-day drop is 21,229 -> 4,251 (about 80%).

corrections.original: JSON search ... about 5 ms per search back to back and 11-15 ms at a keystroke, against 13-14 s for the same program on the CPU as generated JS. Against RegExp in 8 workers it is about even.
corrections.fix: Qualify: 13-14 s is the smallest search program (patterns up to 8 states); a 17-32-state pattern takes about 3 minutes as generated JS. 'About even' with 8 RegExp workers holds back to back only (1.9-6.7 ms vs 4.5-5.2 ms); after a keystroke pause the GPU's 11-16 ms is 2 to 8 times as long. The lab's answer to 'Is the GPU clearly faster?' against workers is 'no'.
